correctness.rationale: All distinct descendants split disjointly by retained ones count 2,1,0. Retaining two yields [x^t]P_aP_bP_c, one yields the union of two integer-position intervals with uncovered-gap corrections, and zero yields one word iff t>=2. Double counting parent/descendant pairs gives the stated conditional sum. Transferring one zero from a gap length u>=v+2 to shorter v changes P_u P_v by a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, and cannot enlarge positive-part one-marker deficits, proving existence of a balanced maximizer. The maximum possible 2-one count requires all gaps at least t, as do disjoint full t-wide 1-one intervals, proving exact saturation length and all extremizers. Independently enumerated 2,145 distinct exact deletion-output sets, checked aggregates through n=11 and maxima/plateau through n=29; exhaustive tests are corroboration only.

final_claim: For all n>=2 and 0<=t<=n binary words with exactly two 1s, the distinct exact-t deletion descendant count is the three-gap coefficient-plus-interval formula. The sum over the fixed-weight-two class is C(t+2,2) C(n-t,2)+t(n-t)^2+C(t,2)(n-t)+1_{t>=2} C(n,2), with balanced finite-length maximizers and a sharp plateau beginning at n=3t+2 (t>=1).
limitations: Binary words with exactly two ones and exactly t deletions; uniform source-word averaging, not random deletion locations.
No claims for arbitrary weight, insertion spheres, or intersections of deletion balls.
